page: Vultr vbm-72c-480gb-gh200-gpu is a dedicated bare metal server built on the NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip architecture. The platform integrates a 72-core arm64 NVIDIA Grace processor running at 3.1 GHz with Neoverse V2 cores, providing 72 dedicated threads without simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 480.0 GB, yielding 6.67 GB of RAM per physical core, while graphics acceleration is driven by an onboard NVIDIA Hopper GH200 GPU featuring 96 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM.

Storage is provisioned via a 960 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one public IPv4 address. The tightly coupled CPU-GPU architecture delivers high computational density within a unified platform, offering qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive artificial intelligence pipelines by eliminating hypervisor overhead. A key architectural tradeoff is the modest 960 GB local NVMe disk volume relative to the extensive 480 GB system memory and 96 GB GPU capacity, necessitating network storage attachments for massive datasets. Additionally, utilizing an arm64 host requires software environments compiled specifically for the AArch64 ecosystem.

This hardware configuration is specifically targeted at demanding accelerated compute tasks. Appropriate workloads include large language model training and inference, generative AI model serving, high-performance computing simulations, molecular dynamics, and parallelized data science workloads that require fast GPU-to-memory interactions.

The server is well aligned for large language model inference, deep learning model training, accelerated data science, and high-performance scientific simulations.
